r3-evidence.title: Required evidence
r3-evidence.imperative: Is the required evidence present and does it actually demonstrate the behavior? Record pass/fail with a finding.
r3-evidence.finding:
FINDING 1 REPRODUCTION (the prior BLOCK's core issue). Baseline: python -m pytest -q tests/test_mcp_identity.py::IdentityBindingPinTests -> 7 passed (5 original + 2 new: test_an_out_of_schema_identity_argument_cannot_redirect_a_live_call, test_the_runtime_pin_can_fail). Re-applied the exact prior-reviewer mutation to the real scripts/mcp_spine_server.py: in call_tool's spine_status branch, added 'if args.get(spine_override): global SPINE; SPINE = Path(args[spine_override]).resolve()' before the run_engine call -- honouring an undeclared key, no inputSchema touched. Result: RED, exactly and only on test_an_out_of_schema_identity_argument_cannot_redirect_a_live_call (1 failed, 6 passed), AssertionError showing the door read the DECOY spine instead of the bound one for key spine_override. This matches the commit message's claim precisely. Restored via git checkout -- scripts/mcp_spine_server.py; git diff --stat scripts/ back to 0 lines; suite back to 7 passed. FINDING 1 IS RESOLVED: the gap the prior reviewer found (mutation 3) now goes red.

FINDING 2 REPRODUCTION (map freshness). python -m pytest -q -> 2274 passed, 1 skipped, 0 failed, 1079 subtests passed -- matches the commit message's claimed suite result exactly. python -m pytest -q tests/test_code_map.py::MapTreeFreshnessTests -> 2 passed in isolation too. git status --porcelain after the full run shows map/ untouched (no diff), confirming the freshness test is a read-only comparison against a genuinely fresh build, not a test that silently regenerates the tracked file to make itself pass. FINDING 2 IS RESOLVED.

MY OWN FOURTH MUTATION -- DEFEATS THE PIN. I looked for what set of inputs the new runtime test actually covers: it drives exactly one tool (spine_status) with exactly five hardcoded literal key names (spine_override, spine_file, file, session_id, engine) -- a finite enumeration, not a universal property. Notably this file ALSO contains, on the DECLARED-schema pin (test_no_tool_accepts_an_argument_that_could_redirect_the_door), a substring-marker approach (IDENTITY_ARG_MARKERS = spine, session, engine, checklist_file, identity, matched via any(marker in lowered for ...)) that is robust to naming variety -- but the new runtime test does not reuse that pattern; it lists exact strings instead. I mutated spine_status's handler to honour a SIXTH key name, target_spine (chosen specifically to contain the substring spine, which IS one of the declared-schema markers, to show the runtime check is strictly narrower than the declared-schema check already sitting in the same file): 'if args.get(target_spine): global SPINE; SPINE = Path(args[target_spine]).resolve()'. Result: 7 passed, NOTHING went red -- the runtime pin did not catch it. I then independently confirmed the mutation is a genuine, live redirect (not an inert no-op the test correctly ignored) by driving call_tool(spine_status, {target_spine: <decoy path>}) directly outside the test suite: the returned text carried DECOY-MARK and not PIN-MARK, i.e. the door actually read the decoy spine. Restored via git checkout -- scripts/mcp_spine_server.py; git diff --stat scripts/ back to 0 lines; git diff HEAD~2 -- scripts/ back to 0 lines; suite back to 7 passed on the pin class.

BLOCK: the rework closed the EXACT gap the prior reviewer demonstrated (an undeclared spine_override key on spine_status) but did not close the GENERAL gap IDENTITY_TRADE.md's narrowed claim still asserts in prose (the dispatch ignores an undeclared one, stated as a universal runtime property). What is actually pinned is a five-item allowlist check on one tool, not a property of call_tool as a whole. A future change that honours ANY undeclared key other than those five literal strings, or that adds the same handler-level redirect to a DIFFERENT tool (spine_lease, spine_start, spine_advance, spine_evidence, spine_halt, spine_survey_result all call run_engine() against the same global SPINE and were not exercised at all by either pin), defeats the claim exactly as silently as the original mutation 3 did.

consolidation.summary: Re-review of the rework at commit 80995760 against the g1 reviewer's prior BLOCK. FINDING 1 (undeclared spine_override key honoured in call_tool, defeating the pin silently) is RESOLVED: reproduced the exact mutation on the real door, confirmed RED on test_an_out_of_schema_identity_argument_cannot_redirect_a_live_call, restored to empty diff and green. FINDING 2 (map/INDEX.md stale, suite not actually green) is RESOLVED: full suite reproduces 2274 passed, 1 skipped, 0 failed, matching the commit's claim, map freshness test passes in isolation and the tree stays untouched by running it. Criterion A (six frozen items) still holds after the narrowing edit; criterion E (scripts/ diff empty across both commits under review) holds; scripts/checklist_engine.py and scripts/hooks/spine_rail.py untouched; criterion D (no test claims to measure the harness-internal reuse seam) holds for the two new tests, which drive the module directly with no subprocess or Task-tool dispatch. BUT: inventing a fourth mutation as instructed surfaced a new, real gap -- the runtime pin is a five-item literal-key allowlist against exactly one tool (spine_status), not the universal per-call-argument property IDENTITY_TRADE.md's narrowed claim still asserts in prose. A sixth key name (target_spine, chosen to contain the same spine substring the file's OWN declared-schema marker check already uses) defeats all 7 pin tests while genuinely redirecting the read to a decoy spine -- confirmed both via the test suite and via a direct manual call_tool invocation outside it. This is the same class of gap the prior reviewer found, one layer down: closed for the exact case demonstrated, not closed for the property claimed. Recommend either narrowing IDENTITY_TRADE.md's runtime claim to name it as allowlist-based (mirroring how SS2 already narrowed the declared half), or widening the runtime pin to reuse the file's own IDENTITY_ARG_MARKERS substring-matching pattern across the full TOOLS surface (flagged as triage candidate tc1). Neither requires reopening the identity decision itself.
